feasibility_reasoning:
The mechanism holds. LH 13.5 core/gather/driver/wait-for-condition.js:422-480 ends the trace at load+1 s plus network-2-quiet and critical-quiet for 1 s, then 1 s of cpu-quiet. That is a strict subset of v2's condition (load+5 s and 5 s with no longtask and no finished resource). gtag could only land in the trace if Lighthouse stayed open more than 4 s with no completed request and no long task, which needs requests stuck in flight; nothing like that exists on / for anonymous visitors. The simulation had 0 of 7 runs with gtag in the trace. The only loader is ConsentScriptInjector.tsx:225-229. The SSR snippet (__root.tsx:491-493) and the dataLayer are unchanged, so there is no hydration, i18n or CLS risk, and the module is already in the entry (__root.tsx:76).

What weakens it:
(1) docs/performance/2026-09-30-critical-boot.md:5 says "do not ... defer work solely beyond the audit window", and prior-art D1 (faza1/raporty/prior-art.md:240) already flags it. The report's own rationale (§0.4) is that the window always lands after the trace ends, so the owner has to sign off.
(2) Possible field INP regression. Today, visitors who interact after about load+3.5 s already have gtag evaluated during idle time. Under v2, anyone who interacts before about load+10 s pays gtag evaluation right after the first interaction.
(3) The cap is visibility-gated, so a tab opened in the background and closed unseen never sends page_view. Today the 8 s cap fires even when hidden.
(4) The gate list is incomplete. gtagLoadPolicy.test.ts:290 (disconnect called once) is outside the :164-270 block and breaks with a second observer. The shared FakePerformanceObserver (:15-31) feeds longTask() to every observer. scheduler.postTask has no typing in TS 5.9.3 lib.dom.
(5) The evidence comes from an inline simulation (exp/inject-proxy.mjs NEW_POLICY), not the proposed code. It listens to wheel instead of scroll, caps at 30 s instead of 20 s, has no visibility gate, and uses getEntriesByType, which the 250-entry buffer caps.
blocking_issues: Conflicts with the project constraint 'do not defer work solely beyond the audit window' (docs/performance/2026-09-30-critical-boot.md:5; prior-art D1). The owner or user must explicitly accept it.

The gtagLoadPolicy.test.ts:290 cancellation test (disconnect toHaveBeenCalledOnce) and the shared FakePerformanceObserver (:15-31) must be reworked for a second 'resource' observer, outside the stated :164-270 block.

The A/B 'new' arm was an inline simulation (wheel instead of scroll, 30 s cap, no visibility gate, getEntriesByType). The real implementation must be re-measured with exp/run-exp.sh before claiming the effect.
The visibility-gated cap drops page_view for background-opened tabs that are never viewed. This must be added to the documented trade-off and to TP-3.
Field INP risk: users who interact between load+3.5 s and load+10 s now get gtag evaluation right after their first interaction. Watch field INP alongside GA4 page_view.
effect_reasoning:
Only TBT moves. TTI is not scored, and gtag starts after observed LCP, outside the LCP graph, so LCP, SI and FCP are unchanged.

Mobile: the host factor from the main-thread ratio is k = PSI 4.2 s / M3 3418 ms ≈ 1.23. That supports the low calib model, not k=1.8. The Lantern gtag tasks at k=1.23 are AW 183→225 (175 blocking), G 69→85 (35) and G 51→63 (13), about 223 ms in total; the observed-task model gives 212. TBT 600→about 385 moves the log-normal score (p10 200, median 600) from 0.50 to 0.698, ×30% = +6 points. The −400 ms / +12 upper end needs k=1.8, which contradicts the main-thread ratio.

Desktop: one PSI run on an overloaded host (5.0 s main thread at 1x vs 0.58 s on M3). The M3 gtag tasks 14/12/41.7 ms give about −283 ms at calib k=6.4 and −122 ms at k=4. The score (p10 150, median 350) goes from 0.13 to 0.21-0.34, i.e. +2…+6 points.

The local A/B +10 does not transfer, because the fake tag's simulated tasks (410/184/180 ms) are about 2.2x production's (183/69/51).

Cheaper or overlapping option: TP-2 (no config AW before marketing consent) removes the AW task, 87% of gtag blocking on M3 (133 of 153). That is about −175 ms and +5 points on PSI mobile, and it also saves real users 200 KB and 185 ms of CPU, with no page_view loss and no audit-window concern. After TP-2, TP-1 adds only about −50 ms. A constants-only version (5000/5000/20000) would very likely match v2 on / at lower cost.
corrected_estimate: PSI mobile TBT −200 to −225 ms (central −215): score from 0.50 to about 0.70, +6 points (range +4 to +8 given PSI TBT variance of 450-760). PSI slow desktop −120 to −280 ms: +2 to +6 points (central +4, low confidence because it rests on one run). If TP-2 (GA4-only before marketing consent) lands first, TP-1's incremental effect is only about −50 ms mobile TBT (+1 to +2 points). The local +10 is not representative.
better_alternative: Do TP-2 first: drop gtag('config', AW) from the SSR snippet and configure it only after marketing consent. It captures about 80% of the TBT gain (the AW task is 133 of 153 blocking ms) and is a real reduction for real users, with no page_view loss and no conflict with the audit-window rule. Treat TP-1 as an owner decision on top. If it is accepted, start with the constants-only version (MIN 5000, quiet 5000, cap 20000) plus the resource observer, and do not gate the cap on visibility so background tabs still report.
